sections.h2: Where to take a deed for recording
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Wayne County Register of Deeds, 400 Monroe, 7th floor, in the Greektown neighborhood of downtown Detroit. The Treasurer's deed certification desk is in that building too, on the 5th floor.

Since October 1, 2025 the office no longer takes walk-ins. Service is by appointment, and nobody can wait on the floor for a cancellation. The day's first slots begin at 8:00 AM and the last begin at 3:50 PM. A 20 minute slot handles up to five documents, while a 45 minute slot is reserved for high volume customers filing five to 25. One person per appointment may enter. The scheduling help line is 313-224-5860, and the recording help line is 313-224-5851.

Mailing documents in is also allowed. Recorded papers come back the way they arrived. An agent who hand delivered them must collect them in person, and mailed ones return to the address typed on the document, which is often the attorney's or the title agent's, not the buyer's.

The fee schedule changed on January 1, 2026, the first rise since 1996. For a deed, mortgage or similar instrument the charge is $26.00 plus a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee, which adds up to $30.00 for each document no matter how many pages it runs.

sections.h2: How the county collects transfer tax
sections.html:
The Register states the formula: $0.55 per $500 of consideration for the county, $3.75 per $500 for the state, which the office also expresses as $8.60 per $1,000. The tax is collected when the deed is filed unless an exemption is noted on it, and accepted forms are cash, check or money order, payable to that office.

Exemptions are listed in MCL 207.526 and, for the county tax, MCL 207.505. A deed claiming one must cite the statute and subparagraph. Typical examples seen in a house sale:

  • consideration below $100
  • a gift deed running down to a son, daughter or grandchild
  • a deed issued in foreclosure or instead of foreclosure
  • a land contract whose title has not yet passed to the buyer
  • a court order with no stated price

Sellers who held a principal residence exemption should also read subsection (u) of the state act. It excuses certain arm's-length sales where the state equalized value never rose above the first value set after the home was built or bought, and a refund can be requested when tax was paid on such a sale.

sections.h2: What payment does the counter accept?
sections.html:
Debit and credit cards work at the counter when the cardholder shows matching ID. So do money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks, corporation checks and law firm checks. Two card brands, American Express and Discover, are refused. Personal checks are turned away at the window yet welcome in the mail, and cards cannot be used for mailed filings.

Each document needs its own check for fees plus any tax. The office is strict about amounts:

  • Underpaying returns both document and check.
  • An overpayment above $25.00 also returns everything.
  • An overpayment of $25.00 or less is kept and not refunded.
  • Several documents on one check travel as a group, and if one fails, all come back.

Title companies handle this routinely. If you are recording a family transfer on your own, work out the exact figure first.

sections.h2: What a deed needs to be accepted
sections.html:
The county posts a checklist and a list of common rejection reasons. The main points are original signatures with names typed, printed or stamped under them, a notary acknowledgment on any real estate deed signed in Michigan, plus the preparer's name and address.

  • Pages meet the office's size, margin, ink and type rules, with a deep blank top margin on page one.
  • The document's title sits on the first line, and the parcel number and street address are shown.
  • A full legal description appears, including plat liber and page or condominium details where they apply.
  • Any Social Security number has its first five digits removed or hidden.
  • A death certificate is an original certified by the clerk, and a court order is certified and sealed.

The register does not furnish blank forms and cannot give legal advice. An attorney is the office's recommendation for drafting.

sections.h2: Why the Treasurer certifies a deed first
sections.html:
MCL 211.135 bars the register from recording until a treasurer's certificate shows the parcel's taxes current for the prior five years. Wayne County requires the Treasurer's stamp on warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and their assignments.

Only originals can be certified. Make a separate appointment with the Treasurer, or send the original by UPS, FedEx or USPS with a check payable to the Wayne County Treasurer and a stamped return envelope. The Treasurer sends it back and you forward it for recording. A document listing more than 25 parcels pays $5.00 plus 20 cents per extra parcel.

Unpaid tax is the usual snag. A bill left unpaid at the local office past the end of February is delinquent from March 1 and then payable only to the county. After a full year it is forfeited, the interest climbs to 1.5% a month, and a $175 foreclosure fee plus $30 in recording charges join the balance.

sections.h2: Booking and timing in a large county
sections.html:
The office calls itself the library of land records for nearly 900,000 parcels, filed by liber and page back to 1703. Wayne County has 814,793 housing units, and 64.8% of homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owned home is $178,500.

At that volume, appointments fill up. Reserve one early when a closing depends on a recorded deed, and ask the title company which of your documents need Treasurer certification beforehand.

sections.h2: How can you find or copy a recorded deed?
sections.html:
You can use the land records website, visit the office, or request a search by mail. The website is open around the clock. A free name search shows a list of recorded documents by grantor or grantee but not the documents themselves. A paid On-Demand Account adds searches by address, legal description, parcel number or liber and page, and printing costs $2 per page. Certified copies are not sold online.

Lobby kiosks allow self-service searching. Current and former service members can get a search of their own property and its copies at no charge with credentials, though businesses are excluded. A mailed request needs a short description, a check payable to the Wayne County Register of Deeds, and the address 400 Monroe, 7th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226. Ask the office which years of images your search needs before you buy an online session.

faqs.q: What does Wayne County charge for one recorded document?
faqs.a: The charge is $30.00, made up of $26.00 plus the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. A warranty deed also needs Treasurer certification at $5.00. The current schedule began January 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I just show up at 400 Monroe to record a deed?
faqs.a: No. Since October 1, 2025 service is by appointment only. Choose record, search or kiosk on the county's calendar, or call 313-224-5860 for help booking.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does Wayne County print per $500?
faqs.a: The county prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, or $8.60 per $1,000. The seller pays at recording unless the deed cites an exemption.

faqs.q: Will the Register of Deeds write my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. The office provides no blank documents and may not give legal advice. It points owners to an attorney who can prepare a deed that meets the recording rules.

faqs.q: What gets a Wayne County deed sent back?
faqs.a: A photocopied signature, no stated price or exemption, wrong margins or type size, a thin legal description, or no treasurer certification. Rejected papers return with the check so you can fix and refile.
